title: Where a population starts decides which peak it climbs
subtitle: A conference talk in the dark twin: a stat tile, a progressive reveal in four steps, the surface at two fixed views, its heat-map twin and a TikZ diagram built step by step
data: illustrative simulation on the analytic landscape w(z1, z2) of examples/python/_common.py; not data
alt: A dark 16:9 deck of 11 frames (14 pages with the diagram's build steps). In an illustrative simulation on a two-peak landscape, most random starts end on the lower peak at fitness 0.72, not on the higher one at 1.00; four populations are revealed one by one, the surface is shown at two fixed views and then as a heat map with the basin boundary.
note: Illustrative simulation, labelled on every slide. Figures by examples/python/talk/make_talk_figures.py, built by examples/latex/talk/build.py. The page is the 160 x 90 mm frame enlarged by 1.764 so the 10 in slide figure and the 28/20/10 pt type sizes hold at 1:1.
